facts.text: This ABC movie was written for soap star Susan Lucci: her 1983 contract renewal for All My Children guaranteed her a primetime TV movie, and ABC commissioned writer Richard Rothstein's script for her.
Michael Berryman and Nicholas Worth were Wes Craven regulars: Berryman in The Hills Have Eyes (and its 1984 sequel), Worth as a henchman-turned-monster in Craven's Swamp Thing.
It first aired on ABC on May 24, 1984, the same year director Wes Craven's A Nightmare on Elm Street hit theaters.
Screenwriter Richard Rothstein later wrote the sci-fi hit Universal Soldier (1992) and created HBO's anthology series The Hitchhiker.
Soleil Moon Frye (Chrissy Winslow) was 8 when Punky Brewster premiered on NBC in September 1984. Producers reportedly weighed about 3,000 girls, including Melissa Joan Hart, for the role.
The film earned a 1984 Primetime Emmy nomination for Art Direction. Meanwhile Susan Lucci herself famously lost 18 straight Daytime Emmy nominations before finally winning in 1999.
Barret Oliver, who plays the Winslows' son Robbie, was also the hero of the fantasy hit The NeverEnding Story, released the same year.
The astronaut suit worn by star Robert Urich came from MGM's wardrobe, the only Hollywood collection of real NASA-style suits. It had no backpack, so the crew built one with a cooling fan.
Patty McCormack (Mary Peterson) was Oscar-nominated for Best Supporting Actress at age 11 for playing the killer child Rhoda in The Bad Seed (1956).
Director Wes Craven's 1978 TV horror Stranger in Our House (Summer of Fear) changed a pet dog to a horse at star Linda Blair's suggestion, since she was an equestrian.
Bill Erwin is also in the cast. He later played Sid Fields, the cranky senior Jerry 'adopts' on Seinfeld.

In the effects shots of the space suit falling into the inferno, the 'actor' is a G.I. Joe doll. Production designer Hub Braden's mother sewed its tiny suit; the doll was spun on a rod in blue screen.
Joe Regalbuto (Tom Peterson) went on to play reporter Frank Fontana on Murphy Brown, then voiced the same character on Ink and Family Guy.
While this aired, Joanna Cassidy (Pat Winslow) was starring in NBC's Buffalo Bill with Dabney Coleman, which won her a Golden Globe and an Emmy nomination.
Star Robert Urich did all his own work in the space suit. No stunt double or other actor stood in for him.
Storyboarding a TV movie is rare. Producers hired illustrator Petko Kadiev to draw the whole script, a visual bible for director Wes Craven, the cinematographer and the effects crew.
The optical effects house, Hollywood Effects, had previously handled effects for the James Bond films through its London unit.
The year this aired, director Wes Craven also made A Nightmare on Elm Street, which he based on news reports of young men who died in their sleep during nightmares.
The film was shot partly on a sound stage at Culver Studios, the old Selznick lot where Gone with the Wind was made. Other locations included Simi Valley, Woodland Hills and Westlake Village.
Pat Padua of Spectrum Culture reads the film as a critique of the 'banal evil' of 80s corporate culture. He finds its casting more interesting than the film itself.
The fire-aisle set heat melted the plastic wall panels and scorched Susan Lucci's costume and hair during retakes. The panels visibly sag on camera.
Critic Lisa Marie Bowman called it 'totally ludicrous but also a lot of fun,' saying Robert Urich is 'properly stolid' while Susan Lucci steals the movie with an over-the-top performance.
Encyclopedia.com's entry sums the film up as Faust meets All My Children in suburbia.
Cinematographer Dean Cundey shot this film. He is best known for John Carpenter's Halloween and later shot Jurassic Park.
The Lightning Bug Movies blog compares the film's mix of tones to The Stepford Wives, The Omen and the final half hour of Star Trek: The Motion Picture.
VideoHound's Golden Movie Retriever warns that fans of Wes Craven's gritty The Last House on the Left, or his polished Nightmare on Elm Street, will be disappointed by this one.
Joanna Cassidy (Pat Winslow) played the replicant Zhora in Blade Runner two years earlier. She also lost the title role of Wonder Woman to Lynda Carter.
Robert Urich starred in a record 15 TV series over his career, per Wikipedia, from S.W.A.T. and Vega$ to Spenser: For Hire, which started the year after this film.
Screenwriter Richard Rothstein practiced law in New York for two years before moving to Los Angeles to write screenplays.
DVD Verdict's Patrick Naugle called the film 'utter tripe' but said he got 'sucked into' it, calling it 'a goofy, hysterically fun mess' best watched with friends.
Production designer Hub Braden suggested a 'Hitchcock twist' ending to set up a Susan Lucci sequel. The producers loved it but feared ABC executives would balk at changing the approved script.
Kevin McCarthy, who plays Mr. Thompson, was the hero of the 1956 Invasion of the Body Snatchers and later turned up in The Howling and Innerspace.
Kevin McCarthy (Mr. Thompson) earned an Oscar nomination for his screen debut as Biff in Death of a Salesman (1951) and later toured for decades in a one-man show as President Truman.
